Run statistics on a data.frame.

Source: R/stats_table.r
stats_table.Rd

A simple interface to lower-level statistics functions: stats::wilcox.test(), stats::kruskal.test(), emmeans::emmeans(), and emmeans::emtrends() on models fitted with stats::lm() or mgcv::gam(). The default test ("emmeans") is parametric; use "wilcox" or "kruskal" for rank-based tests.

Usage

stats_table(
  df,
  regr = NULL,
  resp = attr(df, "response"),
  stat.by = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  test = "emmeans",
  fit = "gam",
  at = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  alt = "!=",
  mu = 0,
  p.adj = "fdr"
)

Arguments

df

The dataset (data.frame or tibble object). "Dataset fields" mentioned below should match column names in df. Required.

regr

Dataset field with the x-axis (independent; predictive) values. Must be numeric. Default: NULL

resp

Dataset field with the y-axis (dependent; response) values, such as taxa abundance or alpha diversity. Default: attr(df, 'response')

stat.by

Dataset field with the statistical groups. Must be categorical. Default: NULL

split.by

Dataset field(s) that the data should be split by prior to any calculations. Must be categorical. Default: NULL

strata

Dataset field with a blocking variable, such as a subject identifier for repeated measures. Must be categorical. When given, regression models (test = "emmeans" or "emtrends") include a random intercept per stratum, fitted with mgcv::gam() as s(strata, bs = "re") (a linear mixed model for fit = "lm" and "log"). Not supported by the rank tests. Default: NULL

covariates

Dataset field(s) to adjust for, such as age or antibiotic use. Each is added to the regression model as a linear term (numeric fields) or a factor (categorical fields), and the reported means, slopes, and differences are adjusted for them: emmeans::emmeans() holds numeric covariates at their mean and averages over the levels of categorical ones with equal weights. Only for test = "emmeans" or "emtrends"; the rank tests can't adjust for covariates. Rows with an NA in a covariate are dropped. A covariate that has the same value in every observation of a comparison (e.g. within a pair of groups) gives an NA row and a warning naming it. Default: NULL

test

Method for computing p-values: 'wilcox', 'kruskal', 'emmeans', or 'emtrends'. Default: 'emmeans'

fit

How to fit the trendline. 'lm', 'log', or 'gam'. Default: 'gam'

at

Position(s) along regr where group means or local slopes are evaluated. Only used by test = "emmeans" with stat.by, and by test = "emtrends" with fit = "gam" (the other combinations test a single, global slope). Default: NULL, which evaluates at one prespecified position: the median of regr (computed within each split.by stratum). A vector evaluates at each position; the returned table then has one row per position, and the p-values are adjusted across all of them.

level

The confidence level for calculating a confidence interval. Default: 0.95

alt

Alternative hypothesis direction. Options are '!=' (two-sided; not equal to mu), '<' (less than mu), or '>' (greater than mu). Default: '!='

mu

Reference value to test against. Default: 0

p.adj

Method to use for multiple comparisons adjustment of p-values. Run p.adjust.methods for a list of available options. The adjustment spans the entire returned table: every combination of split.by strata, stat.by pairs, and at positions. Default: "fdr"

Value

A tibble data.frame with the fields below. The R code used to generate the statistics is in $code.

FieldDescription
.meanEstimated marginal mean. See emmeans::emmeans().
.mean.diffDifference in means (first group minus second).
.slopeTrendline slope. See emmeans::emtrends().
.slope.diffDifference in slopes (first group minus second).
.loc.shiftHodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift between two groups (wilcox).
.pseudomedianHodges-Lehmann estimate of the location (one-sample wilcox).
.h1Alternative hypothesis.
.p.valThe probability, under the null hypothesis, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.
.adj.p.p.val after adjusting for multiple comparisons across the whole table.
.effect.sizeCohen's d effect size. See emmeans::eff_size().
.lowerConfidence interval lower bound.
.upperConfidence interval upper bound.
.seStandard error.
.nNumber of observations used.
.dfDegrees of freedom.
.statWilcoxon or Kruskal-Wallis rank sum statistic.
.t.ratiot statistic: estimate divided by .se.
.edf, .ref.dfEffective and reference degrees of freedom of the smooth term (gam).
.fF statistic for the smooth term (gam).
.r.sqrR-squared (lm); adjusted R-squared (gam).
.adj.rAdjusted R-squared (lm).
.dev.explProportion of deviance explained (gam).
.aicAkaike Information Criterion.
.bicBayesian Information Criterion.
.loglikLog-likelihood of the fitted model.

Tests

Which quantity is tested depends on test and on whether regr and stat.by are given. Rows with an NA in any of the regr, resp, stat.by, split.by, strata, or covariates fields are dropped (with a message).

regrstat.bytest = "emmeans"test = "emtrends"
nonomean of resp vs mu(not allowed)
noyespairwise differences in group means (.mean.diff)(not allowed)
yesnofit = "lm"/"log": the slope's t-test (.slope). fit = "gam": the smooth term's approximate significance (.edf, .f)the slope at at (.slope; global for "lm"/"log", local for "gam")
yesyespairwise differences in group means at at (.mean.diff)pairwise differences in slopes (.slope.diff; global for "lm"/"log", local at at for "gam")

For fit = "log", the slope is with respect to log(regr). mu and alt apply to the mean or slope being tested; they are ignored for pairwise comparisons (always != 0) and for the smooth-term test. Pairwise comparisons fit a separate model to each pair of groups. Without regr, fit is irrelevant: the model is resp ~ stat.by. covariates are added to every model (in the formula, as .cov1, .cov2, ...; the table header names them), so that each of the quantities above is adjusted for them. For example, stat.by = "Treatment", covariates = "Age" compares the groups' means at the average age.

test = "wilcox" runs stats::wilcox.test() (one-sample against mu, or two-sample for each pair of stat.by groups) with exact = NULL, so R chooses an exact or normal-approximation p-value based on the sample sizes and ties. test = "kruskal" runs stats::kruskal.test() across all stat.by groups.

See also

Other stats_tables: adiv_stats(), bdiv_stats(), distmat_stats(), taxa_da(), taxa_stats()

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    biom <- rarefy(hmp50)

    df <- taxa_table(biom, rank = "Family")
    stats_table(df, stat.by = "Body Site")[,1:6]
#> # Model:    lm(.resp ~ .stat.by)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 6
#>    `Body Site`                    .mean.diff .h1   .p.val .adj.p .lower
#>    <chr>                               <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 Mid vagina - Saliva                 83.4  != 0   0.140  0.506  -27.8
#>  2 Anterior nares - Mid vagina        -85.5  != 0   0.161  0.506 -206. 
#>  3 Buccal mucosa - Saliva              60.3  != 0   0.163  0.506  -24.7
#>  4 Anterior nares - Buccal mucosa     -62.5  != 0   0.203  0.506 -159. 
#>  5 Mid vagina - Stool                  73.9  != 0   0.255  0.510  -54.1
#>  6 Buccal mucosa - Stool               50.9  != 0   0.331  0.552  -52.4
#>  7 Buccal mucosa - Mid vagina         -23.1  != 0   0.732  0.873 -156. 
#>  8 Anterior nares - Stool             -11.6  != 0   0.785  0.873  -95.6
#>  9 Saliva - Stool                      -9.47 != 0   0.786  0.873  -78.3
#> 10 Anterior nares - Saliva             -2.12 != 0   0.947  0.947  -65.2

    df <- adiv_table(biom)
    stats_table(df, stat.by = "Sex", split.by = "Body Site")[,1:7]
#> Warning: ! Statistics could not be computed for 1 of 5 comparisons: "Mid vagina / NA".
#> ℹ Message from the underlying tests:
#> • fewer than two groups in this stratum
#> # Model:    lm(.resp ~ .stat.by)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   `Body Site`    Sex           .mean.diff .h1   .p.val .adj.p .lower
#>   <fct>          <chr>              <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Saliva         Female - Male    -0.257  != 0   0.193  0.461 -0.675
#> 2 Buccal mucosa  Female - Male    -0.544  != 0   0.248  0.461 -1.55 
#> 3 Stool          Female - Male    -0.197  != 0   0.346  0.461 -0.657
#> 4 Anterior nares Female - Male    -0.0671 != 0   0.736  0.736 -0.510
#> 5 Mid vagina     NA               NA      NA    NA     NA     NA    

    stats_table(df, regr = "Age", fit = "lm")
#> # Model:    lm(.resp ~ .regr)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 15
#>   .slope .h1   .p.val .adj.p  .lower .upper    .se    .n   .df .t.ratio  .r.sqr
#>    <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <int> <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 0.0159 != 0   0.625  0.625 -0.0490 0.0807 0.0322    49    47    0.492 0.00512
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: .adj.r <dbl>, .aic <dbl>, .bic <dbl>, .loglik <dbl>

    # Repeated measures: a random intercept per subject.
    df <- adiv_table(babies)
    stats_table(df, regr = "Age", stat.by = "Delivery", strata = "Subject", fit = "lm")
#> # Model:    gam(.resp ~ .regr * .stat.by + s(.strata, bs = "re"), method =
#> #   'REML')
#> # A tibble: 1 × 18
#>   `Age (days)` `Delivery mode`    .mean.diff .h1   .p.val .adj.p .lower .upper
#>          <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1          112 Cesarean - Vaginal     0.0835 != 0   0.730  0.730 -0.392  0.558
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: .effect.size <dbl>, .se <dbl>, .n <int>, .df <dbl>,
#> #   .t.ratio <dbl>, .r.sqr <dbl>, .dev.expl <dbl>, .aic <dbl>, .bic <dbl>,
#> #   .loglik <dbl>

    # Adjusting for covariates.
    df <- adiv_table(biom)
    stats_table(df, stat.by = "Sex", covariates = c("Age", "Body Site"))
#> # Model:      lm(.resp ~ .stat.by + .cov1 + .cov2)
#> # Covariates: .cov1 = Age, .cov2 = Body Site
#> # A tibble:   1 × 12
#>   Sex      .mean.diff .h1   .p.val .adj.p .lower .upper .effect.size   .se    .n
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl> <dbl> <int>
#> 1 Female …     -0.210 != 0   0.165  0.165 -0.509 0.0901       -0.468 0.149    49
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: .df <dbl>, .t.ratio <dbl>
